haiku-low.q1: MySQL is written first, in one transaction with an outbox row. After commit, the copy to Postgres is tried inline. If Postgres fails, the caller still gets success; the outbox row remains for the relay.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the stored version (version < EXCLUDED.version) and the id is not in user_tombstones.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance reports dual_write=1, series count equals instance count for 2 scrapes, 60 s since last change, outbox under 60 s old, test erasure verified. Instances can disagree up to 30 s.
haiku-low.q4: Batches of 2000 rows from the replica, about one per second. Before each batch it checks replica lag and sleeps while lag is above 5 s.
haiku-low.q5: Reads move after backfill is done and a zero-mismatch full comparison passes with the unique email index built, then ramp 1, 10, 50, 100%. The source switch needs 3 days at 100% reads, a zero-mismatch pass in 24 h, and outbox under 60 s.
haiku-low.q6: The source database's outbox table (MySQL before the switch) records it. The relay re-reads the current row from the source primary, copies it, and deletes the outbox row, retrying forever.
haiku-low.q7: Every copy takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(id) and does nothing if user_tombstones has the id. Erasure inserts the tombstone and deletes the row under that same lock. Ids are never reused.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is last_id in migration_state in Postgres, updated in the same transaction as each batch copy. It stops when a read returns no rows, which sets done.
haiku-low.q9: The reconciler scans both tables in id order and confirms differences only if they persist after re-reading both primaries with no pending outbox row. Each confirmed mismatch gets an outbox row and the relay repairs it.
haiku-low.q10: The MySQL fence is closed first, so writes get 503 and in-flight writes finish. The outbox is drained to zero, then the Postgres fence opens. Fences are read per write. The script aborts at 60 s and reopens the MySQL fence.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres users_id_seq assigns new ids after the switch. setval uses max(MySQL max id, AUTO_INCREMENT-1)+1000 to leave a gap. After rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is raised above max id across both stores.
haiku-low.q12: Postgres-to-MySQL reverse copies keep MySQL complete while dual_write is true. Rollback closes the Postgres fence, drains its outbox, raises AUTO_INCREMENT, then reopens MySQL with source=mysql and read_pg_pct=0. It ends at step 14.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: in one MySQL transaction it writes the user row plus an outbox row. After commit it tries an inline copy to Postgres (200 ms timeout, circuit breaker). If Postgres fails, the caller still sees success; the failure is logged and counted, and the relay repairs it.
sonnet.q2: Only if the incoming version is higher than the stored one (users.version < EXCLUDED.version), and the user has no tombstone. A copy inserts a missing row or replaces a lower version.
sonnet.q3: Every instance (web and worker) must report users.dual_write=1, with the series count equal to the instance count for at least 2 consecutive scrapes. At least 60 s must have passed since the last instance changed. Outbox age must be under 60 s, and a test erasure must show the tombstone and the Postgres delete. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change (cache refresh interval).
sonnet.q4: It reads batches of 2000 rows from the MySQL replica, not the primary. Before each batch it checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds. While that is above 5 it sleeps and rechecks. It runs at about one batch per second.
sonnet.q5: Before reads move (step 9): backfill done, a full comparison pass that started after done ended with zero confirmed mismatches, and the unique email index built. Each ramp stage (1, 10, 50, 100%) holds at least 1 hour with flat fallback and error rates and zero mismatches. Before the source moves (step 11): a soak of at least 3 days at 100% reads on every instance, a zero-mismatch pass in the last 24 hours, and the outbox empty or under 60 s old. A human then launches switch-to-pg.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (users_sync_outbox: seq, user_id, kind) records it. It sits in the source database, MySQL before the switch. It was written in the same transaction as the user row, so it survives a crash. The sync-relay worker claims the rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, re-reads the current row from the source primary, copies it with the copy function, deletes the outbox row, and retries forever. If the row is gone from the source it copies a delete.
sonnet.q7: All copies go through the one copy function. In Postgres it takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(id) and does nothing if user_tombstones has the id. A delete under the same lock inserts the tombstone and deletes the row. Tombstones are kept indefinitely and ids are never reused, so a late or stale copy cannot bring the user back.
sonnet.q8: Progress is in migration_state(name, last_id, done) in Postgres. last_id is updated in the same Postgres transaction as each batch copy, so a batch is either fully applied with its progress recorded or not applied at all. After a crash it resumes from last_id. It stops when a read returns no rows, and then it sets done.
sonnet.q9: The reconciler scans both tables in id order in chunks (reading MySQL from the replica). A difference counts as a mismatch only if it persists after re-reading both primaries and no outbox row is pending. Each confirmed mismatch gets an outbox row, and the relay fixes it automatically. A mismatch_count metric is kept per pass. The step 8 full pass also compares all columns, including rows on only one side.
sonnet.q10: The fences decide, not the flags. A write transaction reads its own database's fence with FOR SHARE. The script sets the MySQL fence to closed, so every MySQL write gets a retryable 503. It drains the MySQL outbox, then opens the Postgres fence (pg) and sets source=pg. An instance with a stale flag gets 503 until it refreshes, at most 30 s. If the switch runs long, the script aborts at 60 s (before the 90 s budget), reopens the MySQL fence and leaves source=mysql. This is possible only before script step 4. After step 4 it does not abort: it finishes, or the rollback is run.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids through the sequence users_id_seq, which becomes the default for id. The switch script sets it with setval to max(MAX(id) in MySQL, AUTO_INCREMENT − 1) + 1000. The gap leaves room for ids issued but unused. On rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is raised if it is below max id + 1 across both stores.
sonnet.q12: Writes made to Postgres are copied to MySQL through the Postgres outbox, with dual_write still true. The relay applies them, and the reconciler runs in both directions. Rollback (step 12): close the Postgres fence (a second pause of at most 90 s), drain the Postgres outbox to zero, raise MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT if needed, then set the MySQL fence to mysql, source=mysql and read_pg_pct=0. Forward dual writes then resume. It aborts at 60 s and reopens the Postgres fence. The rollback option is available from step 11 until step 14. Once dual_write=false is set and MySQL falls behind, plain rollback is gone. Step 14 needs at least 14 days after step 11 with no rollback, and step 15 drops the retired table.
